intended_object: The canonical isomorphism m/m² ≅ k(m) ⊗_S Ω_{S/K} at a closed point (maximal ideal m) of a finite-type algebra S over an algebraically closed field K. It identifies the Zariski cotangent space of S_m with the fibre of the Kähler differentials. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body composes three maps:
1. The library's general equivalence `IsLocalRing.cotangentSpaceEquivTensorKaehlerOfResidueEquiv`, which works for any local K-algebra whose residue field is K-isomorphic to K and sends the class of x to 1 ⊗ dx. The needed residue-field isomorphism k(m) ≅ K comes from the Nullstellensatz via `residueFieldAlgEquivOfIsAlgClosed`.
2. The base change of the localization isomorphism Ω_{S_m/K} ≅ S_m ⊗_S Ω_{S/K}, which holds because localization is formally étale.
3. `cancelBaseChange`, which collapses k ⊗_{S_m} (S_m ⊗_S Ω) to k ⊗_S Ω.

All the pieces are canonical, so the result is the standard isomorphism. The isomorphism exists more generally at K-rational points over any field, but the library already has that version separately (`cotangentSpaceEquivTensorKaehlerOfResidueEquiv`). This definition is the specialization to closed points of finite-type algebras over an algebraically closed field. In that setting every maximal ideal is rational, so the hypotheses are part of what the statement says and are not an artificial restriction. I found no Mathlib declaration of this isomorphism.
